t.1.14.2: For your sake, to obtain a son, I shall perform the son-bestowing sacrifice, made efficacious in accordance with the prescribed rite by the mantras proclaimed in the Atharvaśiras.
t.1.14.1: Then that wise one, versed in the Vedas, having meditated for a little while and regaining outward awareness, spoke these excellent words to the king.
t.1.14.3: Then, for the sake of a son, the radiant one began that son-bestowing sacrifice, and he made offerings into the fire by the rite as seen in the sacred mantras.
t.1.14.4: Then the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas and the supreme seers assembled according to rule, in order to receive their shares of the offering.
t.1.14.5: Those deities, having assembled in due order in that assembly, spoke a weighty word to Brahmā, the maker of the worlds.
t.1.14.6: O Lord, by your grace a rākṣasa named Rāvaṇa torments all of us through his might, and we are unable to subdue him.
t.1.14.7: O Lord, long ago you, being pleased, granted him a boon; and honoring it always, we forbear everything he does.
t.1.14.8: That evil-minded one torments the three worlds and hates those who are exalted; he seeks to assail Śakra, the king of the thirty gods.
t.1.14.9: Invincible and deluded by the granting of the boon, he oppresses the ṛṣis, the Yakṣas together with the Gandharvas, the Asuras, and the Brāhmaṇas as well.
t.1.14.10: The sun does not scorch him, nor does the wind blow beside him; even the ocean, garlanded with restless waves, does not stir on seeing him.
t.1.14.12: Thus addressed by all the gods, he reflected and then said: "Ah, here is the means devised for the slaying of that evil-souled one."
t.1.14.11: Bearing this in mind, we are in fear of that rākṣasa of terrible appearance; O blessed one, you ought to devise a means for his slaying.
t.1.14.14: Out of contempt, that rākṣasa did not name humans at that time; therefore he is to be slain by a human, and no other death exists for him.
t.1.14.13: By him these words were spoken: 'I am not to be slain by Gandharvas, Yakṣas, Devas, Dānavas and Rākṣasas,' and 'So be it' was said by me.
t.1.14.15: Having heard this pleasing speech uttered by Brahmā, all the gods and great seers then became overjoyed.
t.1.14.16: Meanwhile Viṣṇu, of great splendor, arrived there, and having joined Brahmā, he stood there with his mind composed.
t.1.14.17: Having praised him, all the gods, bowing low, said to him: "O Viṣṇu, out of a desire for the welfare of the worlds, we shall appoint you to a task."
t.1.14.19: There, O Viṣṇu, having become a man, slay in battle Rāvaṇa, the swollen-powered thorn of the worlds, who cannot be slain by the gods.
t.1.14.18: O mighty one, you, in the three wives of King Daśaratha, lord of Ayodhyā, who knows dharma, is generous, and equals the great sages in splendor, in those wives of his who resemble the goddesses Hrī, Śrī, and Kīrti…
t.1.14.20: For that foolish Rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, in the arrogance of his might, oppresses the gods together with the Gandharvas, the Siddhas, and the foremost of sages.
t.1.14.21: Therefore, thoroughly root out that arrogant Rāvaṇa, of mighty power and swollen pride, the enemy of the lord of the thirty gods, who makes beings wail, the thorn of ascetics, the bringer of terror to those who practise austerities.
